title: Change over a conveyor's guide rails for a new carton
instruction: Change the conveyor over for the new carton: move both guide rails in so the carton just fits between them, centred on the white line and parallel to it, then put the carton between the rails on the green outfeed mark.
context: Resetting a packaging line's guide rails for the next product size is a routine changeover, done with the line stopped (locked out before the guides are touched); rails too wide let cartons skew and jam, too tight and they stall. It measures setting a fixture to a size: the rail gap from the carton's width plus a clearance (2 to 12 mm in all, this task's tolerance).
setup: The table top is 74.75 cm above the floor. Two arms 61 cm apart on a table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward and y to the left, in cm. The conveyor's end: a dark grey steel bed with a rubber top, 26 x 22 x 3 cm tall (26 cm along x, from x = 17 to 43), fixed at (30, 0). On it, flush paint marks: a white centre line 4 mm wide along y = 0, the bed's full length, and a green outfeed mark 4 x 2 cm (4 cm along x) at (36, 0). Two aluminium guide rails, bars 24 x 2 x 2.5 cm tall (24 cm along x, 0.32 kg), lie on the bed along x, centred at (30, 8) and (30, -8) (14 cm between their inner faces). The new product, a cardboard carton 6 x 8 x 6 cm tall (6 cm along x, 8 cm along y, 0.3 kg), stands square to the axes on a grey steel staging table (10 x 12 x 1 cm tall, 10 cm along x) at (17, 25).
scoring: Rails set: both resting flat on the bed (released, underside within 2 mm of it, tilted no more than 3 degrees), along x within 2 degrees, each lying within the bed's length (x 17 to 43) and covering x 31.5 to 40.5; measured at both ends of the rails, the gap between their inner faces 8.2 to 9.2 cm (the carton plus 2 to 12 mm) and its middle within 5 mm of the white line; all still (at rest for 1 s): 0.6. Then the carton between the rails on the outfeed mark: upright within 5 degrees, resting on the bed (released, underside within 2 mm), its 8 cm side across the conveyor (turned no more than 10 degrees from square, either way round), its centre within 1.5 cm of the mark's centre, its sides no more than 3 mm past either rail's inner face, still: 0.4 more. Leaving everything as it starts scores 0; rails set but no test carton scores 0.6; the carton counts only with the rails set. An item outside these limits (for example knocked over) does not count as placed; anything the rules above don't cover (for example a part dropped off the table) counts neither way. On real arms, measure the gap and its middle's offset from the line with a tape measure (read to 2 mm) at both ends of the rails, judge position and turn from a top-down photo of the end state, and flatness, tilt and upright from a side photo; the trial ends once everything has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lay the rails back at 14 cm apart and the carton back on the staging table.
fidelity: Approximate. The belt doesn't run (the carton is placed on the outfeed mark, not carried to it) and there is no lockout; the line counts as stopped. The guide rails are loose bars lying on the bed; real ones are clamped on brackets and adjusted with a tool. The simulator gives loose objects rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic).
